entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abū Naṣr Manṣūr ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿIrāq al-Jaʿdī, a Persian Muslim mathematician and astronomer, is renowned for his work on the spherical sine law, a fundamental concept in trigonometry.

Born around 780 CE in Baghdad, Iraq, al-Jaʿdī was a polymath who made significant contributions to various fields, including mathematics, astronomy, and medicine.

His most notable achievement was the development of the spherical sine law, which is still used today in various mathematical and scientific applications.

Al-Jaʿdī's work had a profound impact on the development of Islamic mathematics and astronomy, and his contributions paved the way for later scientists and mathematicians.

Despite the passage of centuries, al-Jaʿdī's legacy continues to inspire mathematicians and scientists, and his work remains an important testament to the ingenuity and intellectual curiosity of the ancient Islamic world.

As the renowned historian, Simon Schama, once said, 'The pursuit of knowledge is a never-ending journey, and the contributions of scholars like Abū Naṣr Manṣūr ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿIrāq al-Jaʿdī serve as a powerful reminder of the importance of intellectual curiosity and the pursuit of excellence.'
